subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase, stagger, or prime-cadence controls for cron `every` schedules and heartbeat, or keep `every` as a fixed anchored interval?
rationale: The remaining change defines public scheduling semantics and persisted config/API shape, and repository policy treats config/default and scheduler surfaces as compatibility-sensitive product decisions.

options.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
options.body: Add one explicit opt-in contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, upgrade tests, and observability before implementation.

options.title: Keep every fixed
options.body: Close or mark the cron `every` portion not planned, preserving fixed intervals while relying on heartbeat phase and cron-expression stagger for anti-herd behavior.

options.title: Accept broader prime mode
options.body: Approve a larger product surface covering prime cadence transforms plus deterministic phase controls across heartbeat and cron, with migration and docs requirements.

recommendation.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit opt-in contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, upgrade tests, and observability before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current cron stagger controls and are the best available owner for the cron scheduling API boundary.
